activity.notes: Historical athlete Milo/Milon of Kroton (Croton), celebrated winner of six Olympic wrestling crowns, the first in the boys' class traditionally dated 540 BCE and the subsequent five in adult competition. The circa 540–520 BCE bounds approximate the recorded festival career rather than personal birth/death dates; ancient evidence disagrees on details of the later chronology and is not turned into invented exact dates. The Croton polis is an existing entity; an athlete active in/representing it was not its sovereign or military ruler. Stories of lifting a bull and other strength feats are treated as later traditions.
